newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before PPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before PPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were narrowly mixed in thin trade with most traders sidelined before today's issue of the U.S. January producer price index (PPI), December business inventories and January industrial production/capacity utilisation data, dealers said on Friday.
The January producer price index is forecast to show an increase of 0.3 percent compared with a 0.5 percent gain reported in December.
Business inventories for December are expected to show a decline of 0.1 percent against November's 0.1 percent gain.
January industrial production is expected to show a gain of 0.1 percent from December's 0.7 percent increase.
Capacity utilisation for January is expected to be around 83.4 percent versus December's 83.5 percent.

"Rates were narrowly mixed this morning amid uncertainty over market direction. There was little impact from Thursday's weekly jobless claims and retail sales figures and most people were sitting on the sidelines," a local dealer said.
"Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the producer price index, business inventories, industrial production and capacity utilisation data," he said.
"But the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend, so I don't think there will be much impact," he added.
In short dates, weekend eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent, but Monday/Tuesday rose 1/8 point to 5-7/16 5-5/16 and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent.

Among term rates, two-months was unchanged from Thursday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8 six-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent.
